name: Gerunds & Infinitives
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to the Gerunds & Infinitives module! This is about deciding between 'To do' and 'Doing'. In French, you almost always use the infinitive (manger, partir) after another verb. In English, you must choose. If you translate directly, you might say 'I finished to work' (Wrong!). This module will teach you the rules.
contrastiveExplanation:
Prepositions + -ing:
English: After ANY preposition (in, on, at, of, for, without), use -ing. (Good at cooking).
French: Uses infinitive (Bon à cuisiner).

Purpose (To vs For):
English: Use 'To' + Verb to explain WHY. (I went to buy bread).
French: Uses 'Pour'. Students often say 'For buy' (Wrong).

Verb Patterns:
Some verbs force -ing (Enjoy, Finish, Stop).
Some verbs force To (Want, Decide, Hope).

commonErrors.frenchConnection: Translating 'pour' as 'for'. Use 'to' + verb for purpose.

commonErrors.wrong: I am tired of to wait.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: French uses infinitive after 'de'. English requires -ing after prepositions.

commonErrors.wrong: I look forward to see you.
commonErrors.correct: I look forward to seeing you.
commonErrors.frenchConnection: The 'to' here is a preposition, not part of the infinitive.

commonErrors.wrong: He stopped to smoke (meaning he quit).
commonErrors.frenchConnection: Confusion between quitting (ing) and pausing to do something (to).

items.feedback: Correct! 'At' is a preposition. Follow prepositions with -ing.
Correct! After 'want', we use the infinitive (to go).
Correct! 'For' is a preposition. Follow with -ing.
Correct! 'Like' is usually followed by -ing (or 'to', but -ing is safer for hobbies).

items.questionText: He went to the shop ___ bread.
items.feedback: Correct! Use 'to' + verb to show purpose (Why he went).
Correct! After 'need', use the infinitive (to leave).
Correct! 'Without' is a preposition. Follow with -ing.
Correct! 'In' is a preposition. Follow with -ing.
Correct! After 'hope', use the infinitive (to see).
Correct! After 'decide', use the infinitive (to stay).
Correct! 'Stop doing' means quit the action.
Correct! 'Before' is a preposition. Follow with -ing.
Correct! Adjective + to + verb (Nice to meet).
Correct! 'Start' can take -ing (or to). -ing is common for ongoing action.
Correct! 'Of' is a preposition. Follow with -ing.
Correct! 'It is no use' is a fixed phrase followed by -ing.

items.questionText: I am responsible for ___ the class.
Can you imagine ___ on the moon?

items.feedback: Correct! He stopped walking IN ORDER TO buy something.
Correct! He quit the habit. 'Stop doing' = Quit.
Correct! 'To' here is a preposition. Prepositions take -ing.
Correct! 'Remember to do' means don't forget a future task.
Correct! 'Remember doing' means having a memory of the past.

items.questionText: The teacher made me ___ the exercise.
items.feedback: Correct! 'Make' (force) takes the base verb (without to).
Correct! 'Let' (allow) takes the base verb (without to).

items.questionText: I used to ___ in Douala (past habit).
items.feedback: Correct! 'Used to' + Base verb = Past habit.
items.subTopic: Used to vs Be used to

items.questionText: I am used to ___ spicy food (accustomed).
items.subTopic: Used to vs Be used to

items.questionText: I regret ___ you that you failed (bad news).
items.feedback: Correct! 'Regret to say/tell' is for bad news now.
Correct! 'Regret doing' is for past actions.
Correct! 'Try doing' means experiment to see what happens. 'Try to do' means make an effort.
Correct! 'Need' + -ing has a passive meaning (It needs to be washed).
Correct! 'Object to' ends in a preposition, so use -ing.
Correct! 'Would rather' takes the base verb.
Correct! Use Gerund for the subject of a sentence (more natural).

items.questionText: Find the error: "I tried to open the window, but I couldn't."
items.feedback: Correct! 'Try to do' means make an effort. It fits here.
Correct! 'Prefer X to Y'. If X is -ing, Y must be -ing.
Correct! Stopped walking TO say hello.

items.questionText: I stopped ___ coffee because of my health.
I look forward to ___ from you.

items.feedback: Correct! Don't forget to do it.

items.questionText: I remember ___ that movie years ago.
We used to ___ in the same class.
items.subTopic: Used to vs Be used to
Used to vs Be used to

items.questionText: I regret ___ you that we are closed.
